learningObjective: Distinguish which decisions belong to compile-time (ahead-of-time lowering, kernel selection, memory planning) and which belong to run-time (dispatch, allocator calls, dynamic shape adaptation).

canonicalClaims.claim: In mainstream ML compilation stacks the compiler is responsible for lowering, optimization, kernel selection and memory planning ahead of time, and the runtime is responsible for dispatch, allocator/stream management and shape-dependent execution paths within the emitted plan.
conditions: The system follows a compile-then-run design (with or without JIT specialization at first call).
The runtime consumes a compiler-produced artifact such as a VM program, plan file, or shared library.
nonImplications: Does not imply that no optimization ever happens at run time; some caches, kernel autotuning and shape specialization occur at run time but do not blur allocator/stream ownership.
Does not imply the boundary is identical across stacks; TensorRT bakes more into the plan than TVM Relax VM, but the compile/runtime split is present in both.

misconceptions.claim: The runtime performs kernel selection and fusion at each invocation.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Fusion and kernel selection are compile-time optimizations; the runtime only chooses among precompiled variants at dispatch time.

misconceptions.claim: The compiler owns the memory allocator and stream scheduler.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Allocator pools and CUDA streams live in the runtime; the compiler emits memory plans but does not call cudaMalloc.
misconceptions.sourceOrEvidence: CUDA Programming Guide; IREE runtime docs

misconceptions.claim: Compiler and runtime are the same component in JIT systems.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Even in JIT-heavy systems the lowering phase (which emits kernels or bytecode) is distinct from the execution phase (which dispatches those kernels).

misconceptions.claim: Runtime memory allocation is negligible so allocator design belongs to the compiler.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Allocator design is a first-class runtime concern (caching allocator, memory pools, fragmentation) and directly affects latency and throughput.
misconceptions.sourceOrEvidence: PyTorch caching allocator; TensorRT runtime memory pools

implementationFacts: IREE separates the iree-compile binary from the iree-run-module runtime
TVM emits a VMExecutable and runs it in tvm.runtime.relax_vm.VirtualMachine
TensorRT emits a serialized plan file consumed by nvinfer1::IExecutionContext
